the-history-of-england-a-study-in-politi: Historian A. F. Pollard traces how England's government grew from medieval kingship into modern parliamentary democracy. Rather than battles and kings alone, he follows the slow change of laws, parliaments, and political ideas across the centuries. Written for serious students, the book explains the forces that shaped the English state and, through it, much of the modern world.
the-romance-of-isabel-lady-burton: Isabel Burton was the devoted wife of the explorer Richard Burton, and this memoir tells the romance of their extraordinary marriage. From dangerous travels in Arabia and Africa to the salons of London, she stood beside one of the Victorian age's most daring figures. Her account is part love story, part adventure — a woman's view of a legendary life.
public-opinion: Walter Lippmann's 1922 classic asks a hard question: can free rule work when voters see the world only in second-hand pictures? He shows how papers, slogans, and fixed ideas shape what men believe. The book that gave us the word stereotype, and still the best first read on news and democracy.
practical-argumentation: George K. Pattee's textbook taught generations of students the art of debate — how to build a case, marshal evidence, and answer opponents. Briefs, refutation, and platform speaking are covered with classroom-tested exercises. For anyone interested in rhetoric or the history of American education, it is a clear window into how persuasion was once taught.
hugh-wynne-free-quaker-sometime-brevet-l: Physician-novelist S. Weir Mitchell sets this Revolutionary War novel in his native Philadelphia. Hugh Wynne, raised a peace-loving Quaker, breaks with his faith to serve on Washington's staff — and finds love amid the struggle for independence. Rich in period detail and quietly moving, it was one of the most admired American historical novels of its time.
the-life-of-the-venerable-mother-mary-of: This biography tells the remarkable story of Marie de l'Incarnation, the Ursuline nun who left France in 1639 to found a convent in Quebec. In the harsh new world of New France she taught Indigenous and French girls, becoming one of Canada's founding mothers of faith. Her life of courage and devotion made her one of the most revered figures in Canadian Catholic history.
country-life-in-canada-fifty-years-ago-p: Canniff Haight looks back half a century to his youth in rural Ontario — the log houses, barn raisings, spelling bees, and winter sleigh rides of pioneer days. His personal recollections preserve details of daily life that official histories miss. Warm and nostalgic, the memoir is a precious record of early Canadian country living.
annette-the-metis-spy-a-heroine-of-the-n: J. E. Collins tells the adventure of Annette, a Métis heroine caught up in the North-West Rebellion of 1885. Part spy story, part frontier romance, it follows her dangerous missions between the warring camps. Popular fiction with a Canadian setting, written when the rebellion's events were still fresh in memory.
inns-and-taverns-of-old-london: Henry Shelley leads readers through the coaching inns and taverns of old London — their signs, their ghosts, their famous patrons from Shakespeare to Dickens. History, anecdote, and topography blend in a book no lover of London should miss. Raise a glass to the city's vanished hostelries.
drusilla-with-a-million: Elizabeth Cooper's lighthearted novel follows Drusilla, whose sudden million turns her quiet life upside down. Fortune-hunters, social climbers, and one honest suitor compete for her hand — and her heart must sort them out. A merry, old-fashioned comedy of wealth and love.
the-hallam-succession: Amelia Barr — the prolific author of historical romances — weaves a tale of inheritance, family pride, and love around the Hallam succession. An unexpected heir must prove worthy of the name and estate. Barr's sturdy storytelling and moral warmth made her books beloved on both sides of the Atlantic.
the-poetical-works-of-mrs-leprohon: Rosanna Leprohon, among the first of French Canada's English singers, gathers her verse of faith, home, and the northern land. Her sweet, godly lyrics were much loved in her day. A gentle book from a true pioneer of Canadian song.
the-boys-of-columbia-high-on-the-gridiro: Graham B. Forbes takes readers onto the gridiron with the boys of Columbia High — hard practices, big games, and the making of a team. School spirit and sportsmanship carry this wholesome football story. A lively period slice of American high-school athletics.
poemata-latin-greek-and-italian-poems-by: Before Paradise Lost, Milton wrote exquisite poems in Latin, Greek, and Italian — gathered here in their original tongues with their classical grace intact. These youthful works reveal the deep learning behind the great English epic. For scholars and lovers of Milton, an essential collection.
the-complete-works-of-artemus-ward-html-: Artemus Ward — Charles Farrar Browne — was America's first great stand-up humorist, and this complete edition gathers his lectures, letters, and sketches. His deliberate misspellings and deadpan absurdity influenced Mark Twain himself. The foundation text of American literary humor. His showman slang and sly wisdom paved the way for Mark Twain and all American humor after him.
a-narrative-of-the-life-of-mrs-mary-jemi: Mary Jemison — captured as a girl in 1758 — lived seventy-five years among the Seneca, and this narrative, taken down in her old age, tells her extraordinary story. Her account of frontier war and Indigenous life is a unique American document. History through unforgettable eyes.
beric-the-briton-a-story-of-the-roman-in: Henty's young Briton Beric stands against the Roman invasion — Boudicca's revolt, the legions, the clash of empires. The boy hero learns war and honor among his own people. Henty at his rousing, instructive best. Against legions and war-galleys the young Briton stands firm, learning courage among his own brave people.
a-march-on-london-being-a-story-of-wat-t: Henty tells the Peasants' Revolt through a brave boy who marches on London with Wat Tyler's host. The storming of the Tower, the king's parley, and Tyler's fall come alive in stirring pages. A vivid, exciting tale of medieval England's great popular uprising.
vestiges-of-the-natural-history-of-creat: Robert Chambers' anonymous Vestiges — published fifteen years before Darwin — dared to suggest that all life had evolved. The book shocked, fascinated, and prepared Victorian minds for the Origin of Species. A landmark of science, brave and brilliant. Though published without a name, its daring idea shook Victorian England and paved Darwin's way.
linda-condon: Joseph Hergesheimer's novel follows Linda Condon, a beautiful, enigmatic woman, through the Jazz Age's glittering world. His jeweled prose made him the stylist of his generation. A shimmering portrait of an era and its heroine. Her strange, cool beauty haunts these pages like a half-remembered dream.
species-and-varieties-their-origin-by-mu: Hugo de Vries, the great Dutch botanist, argues that new species arise by sudden mutation — his famous theory that challenged Darwin. His experiments with evening primroses made history. A landmark of genetics. His primrose experiments opened the modern study of how species change.
archibald-malmaison: Julian Hawthorne's strange tale of Archibald Malmaison — a man who becomes another — blends mystery and the supernatural. His most famous story still chills. A classic of American weird fiction. Identity itself dissolves in this uncanny tale of transformation. Hawthorne's son proves a worthy heir to the family gift for the strange.
how-to-prepare-and-serve-a-meal-and-inte: Lillian Lansdown shows the plain housewife how to set a fair table and keep a pretty home — what to cook, how to serve, and how to make rooms cheerful. Her kind, clear counsel aided many a young bride. A sweet relic of old domestic art.
five-lectures-on-reincarnation: Swami Abhedananda lectures on reincarnation — the soul's long pilgrimage through many lives — with Vedantic clarity. His five talks brought the old doctrine home to Western minds. Lucid Eastern wisdom, gently taught. East and West meet in his learned talks. Seekers after truth will find here a clear and kindly guide.
john-james-audubon: John Burroughs, himself a prince of nature writers, profiles John James Audubon — the woodsman-artist who painted America's birds in all their wild glory. His vivid life of the great naturalist does full justice to a restless genius. A fine double portrait by a master hand.
the-writings-of-john-burroughs-volume-05: John Burroughs' Pepacton — sketches of his beloved Catskill home waters — shows the great naturalist at his most intimate and happy. Trout streams, summer days, and woodland musings fill these pages. Burroughs' Delaware County book, treasured by his readers. Slabsides' neighbors will recognize every stream and hill.
windy-mcpherson-s-son: Sherwood Anderson's Windy McPherson's Son follows Sam McPherson from an Iowa boyhood to Chicago business success — and to the disillusion that follows. His first novel already shows the brooding power of the Winesburg master. A striking and original American debut.
the-duke-of-stockbridge-a-romance-of-sha: Edward Bellamy's Duke of Stockbridge romances Shays' Rebellion — the Massachusetts uprising of 1786 — with love, adventure, and the young republic's growing pains. His early historical novel already shows the reformer's fire. A stirring tale, well told. Debt-ridden farmers and Boston grandees clash in his lively pages.
the-lady-of-the-decoration: Frances Little's Lady of the Decoration sends an American girl to teach in Japan, and her letters home charmed a nation. East meets West in a romance of humor, insight, and goodwill. The book became one of the early twentieth century's best-loved bestsellers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aaron: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on Aaron — brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel — recounts his life from the Exodus to the golden calf. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abaddon: This 1913 Catholic reference piece on Abaddon — the angel of the pit named in Revelation — looks at what the Bible and old writers say of him. Anthony Maas pulls the proof texts together. Students of Revelation will find it a handy place to start.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-corn: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Cornillon — the Belgian house of St. Juliana and the feast of Corpus Christi — records its holy fame. Francis Martin Geudens tells its story. A devout reference on a shrine of the Blessed Sacrament.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abdias-of-bab: A 1913 entry on Abdias of Babylon — the supposed author of an apostolic history, long proved spurious. John Joseph A'Becket sorts fact from fable. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abdication: A 1913 entry on abdication in church law — when popes, bishops, and abbots may lay down office. William Fanning states the rules with care. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abduction: This 1913 reference piece on abduction in canon law — the crime of carrying off, and its penalties. P.M.J. Rock sets out the old rules. Marriage law and church courts meet here. A technical but clear entry. Its canons guarded maids, wives, and novices alike.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abjuration: A 1913 entry on abjuration — the solemn giving up of heresy before the Church. Andrew Meehan explains the old forms. Recanting heretics knelt to swear it. Church law on returning to the fold. Galileo's famous kneeling was an abjuration of sorts.
